title: Surveillance
body:
**Surveillance** is observation exercised by an institution, where [[Data Privacy]]
concerns data collected by a service, and the course separates it from [[Data Privacy]]
because the actor and the remedy differ.

The capability has changed in kind. Following one person once required a person doing the
following, which limited how many could be watched at a time. Recording every transaction,
location and message is now the cheaper option compared with deciding what to discard, so
comprehensive collection happens by default and targeting happens afterwards by query.

The **chilling effect** is the consequence the course emphasises. Knowing that observation is
possible changes behaviour whether or not anybody is watching, so people avoid searching for
some topics, saying some things and associating with some groups. The harm falls on people who
were never investigated and never knew, which makes it invisible to any measure of whether the
surveillance caught anybody.

That structure defeats the usual defence that somebody with nothing to hide has nothing to
fear, since the cost is imposed on the entire population in advance and the benefit accrues in
specific cases afterwards. It is a [[Utilitarianism|utilitarian]] calculation with a diffuse
cost and a concentrated benefit, which is the mirror image of the problem in
[[Automation and Job Displacement]].

Encryption is the technical response, and it is why the policy debate in [[CRYPTOGRAPHY]] about
lawful access keeps returning.
